name: Costa Rica Rainforest
tagline: Biodiversity Hotspot — Where Two Oceans Meet
intro: Costa Rica packs extraordinary biodiversity into a small country — covering less than 0.1% of the Earth's surface, it contains nearly 5% of all known species. From misty cloud forests to Pacific surf breaks and Caribbean mangroves, it offers a stunning combination of wildlife encounters and adventure experiences.

signatureExperiences.title: Corcovado Expedition
signatureExperiences.description: Venture deep into Corcovado National Park, described by National Geographic as the most biologically intense place on earth.

signatureExperiences.title: Pacific Surfing
signatureExperiences.description: World-class breaks at Nosara, Santa Teresa, and Pavones suit all levels, with warm water year-round.

signatureExperiences.title: Night Walk
signatureExperiences.description: After dark, the rainforest transforms. Red-eyed tree frogs, kinkajous, and fer-de-lance snakes emerge in the torch-lit canopy.

signatureExperiences.title: Turtle Nesting
signatureExperiences.description: Between July and October, olive ridley turtles arrive in mass-nesting events (arribadas) on Pacific beaches — a truly overwhelming spectacle.

wildlifeHighlights.notes: Once threatened, macaw populations have recovered dramatically and are commonly seen in Carara and Corcovado.
Corcovado is one of Central America's last jaguar strongholds; patience and expert guidance are essential.
The waters off the Osa Peninsula are a humpback whale breeding ground, visited by both northern and southern hemisphere populations.

lodging.name: Lapa Rios Lodge
lodging.description: Perched above the rainforest canopy on the Osa Peninsula, adjacent to a 1,000-acre private nature reserve.

lodging.name: Nayara Springs
lodging.description: Individual adult-only villas with private volcanic spring pools, adjacent to Arenal Volcano National Park.

bestTimeToVisit: December–April (dry season on Pacific coast); September–October for turtle nesting
